# Proposed relationship audit

## Scope and result

Read the Phase 2 `all-fresh-candidates-master.jsonl`, the proposed projection, its generated JSONL, and the related withheld rows. The master contains 147 unique candidate records. The proposed graph contains 2,467 rows: 1,307 nodes and 1,160 relationships. Every row is `PROPOSED_NOT_APPROVED` with medium projection confidence. The relationships are 724 `MENTIONS`, 289 `SOURCED_FROM`, and 147 `IN_CATEGORY`. No `IN_PHASE` or `HAS_THEME` relationships were emitted; the master has no populated `phase` or `keywords` fields.

The projection keeps entities candidate-local: every relationship starts at that candidate's `proposed:{candidate_id}` root and targets a node with the same `origin_candidate_id`. There are no `Entry` nodes, `entry_number` properties, or `entry:` IDs in the proposed graph. All 1,448 structured evidence tuples for people tags, organization tags, categories, and source URL fields match Phase 2 exactly; no tuple is missing or added. Candidate roots preserve the Phase 2 title as `display_name`, event date, descriptions, allegation classification, and uncertainty. Each root says human editorial approval has not been granted; each relationship basis says it is review-only and not an approved assertion. The narrative fields remain candidate text, including allegations, with uncertainty copied through rather than resolved by the projection.

## Cross-link audit

All 110 proposed-to-canonical withheld records exactly match the Phase 2 `related_entry_numbers` values by `(candidate_id, target number)`: no missing, added, or duplicated pairs. The 110 references come from 56 candidate records and identify 97 distinct target numbers; every target number appears in the canonical entry-number manifest. Each reference is retained only as a `PROPOSED_NOT_APPROVED` withheld ambiguity with `requested_type: RELATES_TO`; none becomes a proposed graph relationship. The `entry:N` value appears only in `possible_target` on those withheld records.

## Diverse relationship examples

These examples compare emitted edges with the exact structured fields that produced them. They show what the projection records and the uncertainty it preserves; they do not independently verify the cited sources or underlying events.

1. **`expanded-20260820-bessent-regime-collapse`** — Phase 2 `people_tags` are Scott Bessent and Donald Trump; `organization_tags` are U.S. Treasury and CNBC; `category` is Foreign Policy; `sources[0].url` is Reuters: `https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-treasury-secretary-bessent-hold-press-conference-iran-on-monday-2026-08-20/`. These yield only `MENTIONS`, `IN_CATEGORY`, and `SOURCED_FROM`. Its classification is `mixed`, and its uncertainty says regime collapse was a forecast, not a demonstrated outcome.
2. **`expanded-20260821-usps-final-rule`** — `people_tags`: Donald Trump; `organization_tags`: U.S. Postal Service; `category`: Election Interference; source URLs are the Federal Register rule and the Congressional Research Service page (`https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/26/2026-17238/ballot-mail-for-federal-elections`, `https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF13297`). The graph emits one `MENTIONS` per explicit tag, one `IN_CATEGORY`, and two `SOURCED_FROM` edges. The candidate's uncertainty expressly says finalizing the rule does not establish ballots were refused.
3. **`fresh-20260826-raskin-1789`** — `people_tags`: Jamie Raskin, Donald Trump Jr., Omeed Malik, Christopher Buskirk; `organization_tags`: 1789 Capital and House Judiciary Committee Democrats; category: Government Corruption. Its source URLs are the committee letter PDF and Guardian report (`https://democrats-judiciary.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/democrats-judiciary.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/2026-08-26-raskin-to-malik-buskirk-trump-jr-1789-capital-re-insider-access.pdf`, `https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/27/democrats-investigation-trump-jr-1798-capital`). The proposed edges remain `MENTIONS` / `SOURCED_FROM` / `IN_CATEGORY`; uncertainty says the minority-party request is not a subpoena or a proven corruption finding.
4. **`oct2026-2026-08-30-epa-flame-retardant-data-manipulation`** — classification: allegation; `people_tags`: Donald Trump and Lee Zeldin; `organization_tags`: Environmental Protection Agency and California Department of Justice; category: Environmental Destruction. The source URLs are The Guardian, California Attorney General, and Inside EPA. They produce only the structured `MENTIONS`, `SOURCED_FROM`, and `IN_CATEGORY` edges. The uncertainty attributes the “manipulation” characterization to advocates/researchers and notes the lack of an independent audit or located EPA response.
5. **`oct2026-2026-10-22-wind-turbine-executive-order`** — classification: established; `people_tags`: Donald Trump; `organization_tags`: Department of Commerce and Office of the U.S. Trade Representative; category: Environmental Destruction. Sources are the White House proclamation, Bloomberg, and CNBC-TV18 (`https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/10/adjusting-imports-of-wind-turbines-and-their-parts-and-components-into-the-united-states/`, `https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/trump-punts-on-wind-turbine-tariffs-allows-180-days-for-talks`, `https://www.cnbctv18.com/world/trump-delays-us-tariffs-on-wind-turbines-orders-trade-talks-and-review-in-180-days-20017577.htm`). The candidate retains uncertainty that the national-security findings are the administration's determination and were not independently verified in the reviewed reporting.
6. **`oct2026-2026-10-23-starlink-ukraine-congressional-probe`** — classification: allegation; `people_tags`: Donald Trump and Elon Musk; `organization_tags`: SpaceX, The White House, and U.S. House of Representatives; category: National Security Violations. Its sources are CNBC, Reuters, and Associated Press (`https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/starlink-ukraine-musk-trump-congress.html`, `https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/order-limit-starshield-ukraine-came-inside-white-house-sources-say-2026-10-15/`, `https://apnews.com/article/starlink-starshield-ukraine-russia-trump-vance-musk-1a9279f37cfd4d2a65c8ce4cc3af6f41`). The projection records explicit mentions and source/category links while preserving the unresolved dispute over who ordered the restriction and whether service was fully restored.

## Provenance follow-up and limits

An initial read found that Source nodes carried `publisher` and `date_published` without provenance for those specific fields. The coordinator updated the projection and regenerated its output. The current output now includes `sources[i].publisher` and `sources[i].date_published` provenance, plus the other structured source-record fields, for every source node. Check: zero missing direct provenance across 558 populated publisher/date values on 289 Source nodes. Candidate roots also now include direct provenance for title, date, descriptions, allegation classification, uncertainty, and the optional allegation-status note.

This was a local file audit with read-only inspection and in-memory checks; no network, credentials, database writes, or apply/import operation was used. The audit checks projection fidelity and safe relationship shape, not source availability, the truth of claims, or editorial approval.
